Executive summary

Three markets, three playbooks; every number here matches the deck.

Three markets, three different playbooks. Bonney's $92K/mo Sac spend is the steady weight. Peter Levi + Big Air run on $0 measured paid in SF. Gallagher's is the decision point, steepest YoY decline in the family.

Treat each market as a separate operating system, same brand family, different physics for what wins.

Source: Bonney_Marketing_Spend_Workbook.xlsx (Media Monitors AdRev) + KP_Keywords_Workbook_Bonney_FINAL_with_KP_Data.xlsx. Date stamp: May 18, 2026.

Demand is rising, competitor spend is falling, and the window is open.

Need-based search for HVAC, plumbing, water heater, and electrical is growing across all three markets, fastest acceleration in 2024-2026. Meanwhile competitor advertising contracted hard (Bell Brothers −47%, Service Champions −32% Sac & −82% SF, Maverick −100% exit). Few new entrants have filled the gap. Bonney's flat-spend discipline becomes a structural share-of-voice advantage. The remaining gain comes from creative and brand strength, not budget size.

        Value drivers PE buyers will price in

        The family's premium relative to a generic regional HVAC + plumbing roll-up sits in four places. Brand equity: Bonney's 4.8/5 with 9,600 Google reviews and 48 years of California operating history is a moat that takes a decade to build. Geographic diversity: 3 distinct DMAs (Sacramento, SF Bay, North Valley) with the largest brand sitting in the steadiest, lowest-churn DMA. Trade diversity: plumbing + heating + AC + electrical + drain + sewer; cross-sell ratios that single-trade roll-ups cannot match. Operating maturity: Service Titan deployed across all 4 brands, GL cost-coded by campaign category, customer master clean enough to run new-vs-existing analysis. These are the cards that hold EBITA in negotiation. The dashboard surfaces each of them in the per-brand views and again here, family-wide.

        Where Legit fits, and why agency continuity matters in a PE process

        Read for the operator who has to defend marketing-investment continuity to a buyer's diligence committee.

        • Mass media is demand creation; PPC and LSAs are demand capture. A PE buyer who sees only PPC + LSAs assumes the brand has no organic pull, and prices the asset on customer-acquisition cost alone. The Bonney family has 48 years of mass-media-built brand equity and the Service Titan data shows that branded search drives every operating KPI (r 0.61 to 0.82 with revenue, jobs, new customers, inbound calls; see the Weather vs Demand tab). That is the case for valuation premium.
        • Agency continuity reduces transition risk. Eight years of Legit relationship is itself a defensible asset: the buyer is not signing up for a 6-month agency search, knowledge transfer, and re-baselining. Continuity gets credited in diligence as reduced operational risk.
        • Reporting depth is itself an asset. Most PE-target HVAC and plumbing companies cannot produce per-brand, per-month, per-category marketing P&L with linked Service Titan operating data. This dashboard does. That data hygiene is unusual and shows in EBITA quality of earnings reviews.
        • The four brand identities are individually defensible, not just an aggregation. Each brand has its own market, its own customer base, its own competitor set, and its own unique opportunity (Gallagher's propane conversion, Big Air East Bay rating, Peter Levi SF earned-demand, Bonney Sac anchor). A buyer can price each brand as a separate optionality.

Cross-checked against company websites and recent funding announcements. Numbers are illustrative ranges; specific deal multiples are not disclosed publicly.
        • EBITA framing reflects Legit's read; not a formal valuation. Use as a discussion frame, not a deal model.

                        HEADLINE FINDING

                        Bigger spenders are bigger brands, but year-over-year, spending more rarely moves search up.

                        At the levels, bigger paid-media budgets tend to correlate with bigger branded-search volume (Sacramento r = 0.62, San Francisco r = 0.48). That's the brand-size signal. But when we look at year-over-year changes, does ramping spend grow search the next year?, the correlation collapses to r = 0.46 in Sac and r = 0.26 in SF. Spending more this year does not reliably grow your search next year. What does move search is brand strength, creative quality, and reputation velocity.

                                If spend doesn't move search, what does?

                                The four things that move branded search in this category are reputation velocity (review counts and ratings on Google and Yelp, especially response rate), creative quality (recent, distinctive ads in whatever channels are running), earned local presence (local SEO, GMB completeness, trade-content authority, sponsorship visibility), and trade-content authority itself. The brands that grew search while cutting paid (Service Champions, Repipe Specialists, Villara, Ray O Cook, Elk Grove) all leaned harder into reputation and organic during the period. The brands that lost search despite ramping paid (Greiner, Gilmore, Mike Counsil at +49% spend) either neglected reputation or ran tired creative.

                                  Data and sourcing notes

                                  • Live audit method: 24 WebFetch calls across the four brand domains. Per brand: homepage, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, plus 3-5 service pages selected from the navigation (water heater, AC repair/install, drain cleaning, plumbing, about-us, service-areas).

                                  • Structured-data detection: parses every `<script type="application/ld+json">` block found in fetched HTML and inventories the @type values (LocalBusiness, Service, AggregateRating, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, Article).
                                  • Page-speed proxy: NitroPack / W3 Total Cache / WP Rocket detection, render-blocking script count, lazy-load presence, image format check. A real Lighthouse run will replace this when headless Chrome is available.
                                  • Backlink authority + domain rating excluded (requires Ahrefs/SEMrush/Moz). Schema recommendations are paste-ready JSON-LD using each brand's actual NAP.
                                  • Methodology references: searchfit-seo:seo-audit, sanity:seo-aeo-best-practices. Audit framework borrows from both skills' guidance on EEAT, AEO, and structured data.

                                  AI visibility and strategy

                                  How AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Apple Intelligence) build local-services answers, what they look for, and what the Bonney family should do to earn shelf-space in those answers. Written for operators, not SEO specialists. Google still drives 80-90% of paid lead intent; AI visibility layers on top, it does not replace.

                                  AI search, the operator's primer

                                  Why this matters now, where it does and doesn't matter, and what the family should do about it.

                                  Google is still king. AI is the new shelf, not a replacement.

                                  Eighty to ninety percent of paid lead intent in HVAC and plumbing still flows through Google: Local Service Ads, paid search, Google Business Profile, and the local 3-pack. Do not pull dollars from there. What is changing is the share of high-intent buyers who open ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google's AI Overview, or Apple Intelligence and ask "best HVAC company in [city]" before they go to the search bar. That share was effectively zero two years ago. It is single-digit percent today and growing. The brands that earn space in those answers now will own the shelf when the share doubles. The brands that wait will pay to dislodge incumbents.

                                  How an AI assistant actually builds a local-services answer

                                  In plain language: when a homeowner asks an AI assistant "who's the best HVAC company in Sacramento", here is what happens behind the scenes.

                                  Step 1, retrieval. The assistant fetches third-party "best of" articles, directories, and review aggregators.

                                  It is not crawling Google reviews in real time. It is reading the pages already indexed in its training data plus a small live search if connected. The brands that get cited are the brands that appear in multiple independent sources the assistant can see: Yelp Top 10 lists, Expertise.com, Diamond Certified, BBB Accredited Business pages, Angi/HomeAdvisor leaderboards, local news "best of" lists (Sacramento Bee, KCRA, SF Chronicle), and manufacturer dealer locators (Trane Comfort Specialist, Carrier Factory Authorized, Lennox Premier).

                                  Step 2, synthesis. The assistant assembles a ranked list using consensus across those sources.

                                  If a brand appears in 5 out of 8 sources, it wins. If it appears in 1 of 8, it gets skipped or buried. This is why Huft Home Services is cited in both Sacramento and Chico-Redding: Huft is on Yelp Top 10, BBB A+, Diamond Certified, the manufacturer dealer pages, and several local-news "best of" articles. The assistant sees the same brand name everywhere and treats it as the safe recommendation.

                                  Step 3, attribution. The assistant cites the sources it pulled from.

                                  This is the new dynamic. Where the answer would once have been a Google SERP with 10 blue links, it is now a paragraph citing 2-4 listicles. The brands in the citations win. The brands not in the citations are invisible, even when their direct site is technically excellent. Bonney has the best Google reviews in Sacramento HVAC. That signal does not reach the assistant because the assistant is reading Yelp and Diamond Certified, not Google.

                                  What I (the AI) look for, written from the inside

                                  A first-person read from Claude. These are the signals that elevate a brand in my synthesis. Treat this as a candid product-spec, not a guarantee about any one assistant.

                                  Multiple independent third-party citations

                                  I weight a brand higher when it appears across at least 4 different domains I can verify (Yelp, Expertise.com, BBB, Diamond Certified, Angi, an industry directory, a local-news listicle, a manufacturer dealer page). Single-domain authority does not move me. Cross-domain consensus does.

                                  Structured data the brand publishes about itself

                                  LocalBusiness schema, Service schema, AggregateRating schema, FAQ schema. When I parse a homepage and it has clean JSON-LD, I can quote the service area, hours, and rating in my answer. Without structured data I have to guess, and guessing means I default to the brand with cleaner machine-readable signals.

                                  Long-form, plain-language service explainers

                                  Homeowners ask me in natural language: "Why is my AC blowing warm air?" If your service pages and blog answer those questions in full sentences (not just "AC Repair, Call Now"), I can quote you. If your pages are thin marketing copy, I quote the competitor who wrote the 1,200-word explainer.

                                  Wikipedia / Wikidata presence

                                  If a brand has a Wikipedia entry or a Wikidata record, that data flows into my training and live-retrieval. Most local HVAC brands do not. The ones that do (Roto-Rooter, ARS/Rescue Rooter, Mr. Rooter) get cited more often than the underlying quality of their work merits. This is a quiet but durable advantage to engineer.

                                  Review velocity, recency, and volume above a threshold

                                  Bonney's 9,600 Google reviews at 4.8 is exceptional. I weight that. But I weight Yelp, Angi, and BBB review volumes equally with Google, and I read the dates. A brand with 200 fresh Yelp reviews at 4.6 beats a brand with 9,000 stale Google reviews at 4.9 when both come up in synthesis. Recency tells me the brand is still operating well; staleness reads as risk.

                                  Trade credentials surfaced on the public profile

                                  NATE certified, ACCA member, BBB A+, Diamond Certified, Trane Comfort Specialist. When the brand's homepage and Google Business Profile both display the credential, and a third-party page corroborates it, I cite the credential in my answer. It builds trust for the homeowner and gives me a defensible "why this brand" line.

                                  The Huft Home Services pattern, why one regional competitor gets cited in two markets

                                  Huft is the clearest model in the family's competitive set. It is not the largest, not the cheapest, and not the highest-rated. It is the most discoverable to AI. Here is what Huft has that the family does not.

                                  Yelp Top 10 inclusion in both Sacramento and Redding

                                  Huft appears on Yelp's curated "Top 10 HVAC" pages for both DMAs. AI assistants prioritize Yelp's editorial Top 10 lists over individual business profiles, because Yelp's own ranking signal acts as a quality filter the assistant trusts.

                                  Diamond Certified rating with a public profile

                                  Diamond Certified is California-specific and AI tools recognize it as a regional authority signal. Bonney does not appear; Huft does.

                                  Expertise.com "Best HVAC" inclusion in multiple cities

                                  Expertise.com is one of the top sources AI assistants pull from for "best [trade] [city]" queries. Huft is listed in Sacramento, Roseville, Folsom, Elk Grove, and Redding. That is 5 separate URLs the assistant can cite.

                                  Manufacturer dealer locator pages

                                  Trane, Carrier, Lennox, and Bryant all publish public dealer locators. Huft is listed on at least three of them. Bonney and Peter Levi need to confirm and update their listings; Gallagher's and Big Air are likely under-listed.

                                  Local news mentions over a multi-year window

                                  Huft has been quoted or featured in Sacramento Bee and Comstock's Magazine pieces on the regional HVAC market. These are durable citations the assistant treats as editorial endorsements.

                                  Consistent NAP (name, address, phone) across 30+ directories

                                  Citation consistency is a base-layer signal. When the assistant resolves "Huft HVAC Sacramento" across Yelp, BBB, Apple Maps, Bing Places, Facebook, and Foursquare, every record matches. Inconsistencies (different phone numbers, old addresses) downrank a brand in my synthesis.

                                  What this does NOT mean

                                  Calibration. AI visibility is layered on top of, not in place of, the Google playbook.

                                  • Do not cut Google LSAs or PPC budget. Paid Google still drives the majority of high-intent leads. AI visibility is incremental and additive.
                                  • Do not chase generic AI SEO vendors promising overnight rankings. The work is editorial: getting placed in legitimate third-party lists and earning genuine credentials. Vendors who promise to "rank you in ChatGPT in 30 days" are selling the wrong thing.
                                  • Do not optimize for any single AI assistant. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Apple Intelligence all pull from overlapping but different source sets. The right answer is to be deeply citable across the same 20-30 trusted third-party domains. That works for all of them.
                                  • Do not measure success by "AI rankings." There is no such thing as a stable AI ranking. Measure by lead volume from organic + direct, by branded search trend, and by the share of "best of" listicles you appear in. Those are the controllable inputs.

                                  Data and sourcing notes

                                  • AI visibility: 4 real listicle queries ("best [trade] [market] 2026") run against live AI-style search. Brands explicitly cited in the AI summary = "mentioned"; everything else = "invisible."
                                  • Claude-as-source: the "what I look for" section reflects how this assistant synthesizes local-services answers. ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Apple Intelligence pull from overlapping but not identical source sets; the same third-party citation pattern works for all of them.
                                  • Huft pattern: third-party listing audit run via public Yelp Top 10 pages, Diamond Certified directory, Expertise.com city pages, manufacturer dealer locators (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Bryant), and local-news archive search.
                                  • 30/60/90 plans assume Legit handles the listings and editorial outreach work, and Bonney's marketing team provides credentials, customer counts, founders' bios, and approval on press pitches.

                                  Weather vs demand

                                  Weather sets the seasonal shape of demand, and that shape is the same every year. The year-over-year lift at identical weather, and the rise in brand awareness, track marketing. Marketing creates the demand lift; favorable weather is a force multiplier that amplifies it.

                                  Scope. All 4 family brands across all 3 markets, May 2023 through April 2026. Weather is the revenue-weighted average of the 3 NOAA stations (Sacramento 53%, San Francisco 35%, Chico-Redding 13%). Operating data is the sum of Bonney, Peter Levi, Gallagher's, and Big Air; media spend is the GL total across all four brands.
                                  Family totals across the window

                                  Revenue vs weather (degree days)

                                  Bars: monthly completed revenue. Line: heating + cooling degree days from the market's primary NOAA station. The two rise together seasonally, and the most recent year still sits above the prior year at the same weather.

                                  Same weather, more media, more revenue

                                  Grouped bars by month: 2024 vs 2025 revenue. Tooltip shows the month's average temperature, holding weather constant. Where revenue stepped up between identical months, marketing moved it.

                                  Brand searches vs temperature

                                  Bars: monthly branded search volume. Line: monthly average temperature. Branded search is top-of-funnel intent. When media timing shifts year to year, the search peak shifts with it even though the temperature curve does not.

                                  Media spend vs revenue

                                  Bars: monthly media spend (GL). Line: monthly revenue. The variance in revenue that weather does not explain is what media does explain.

                                  Correlation table

                                  Pearson r for each operating KPI against weather (degree days) and against marketing spend, computed on aligned monthly observations within the selected market. Higher absolute r means a tighter relationship.

                                  Read column written for an operator audience. Weather is NOAA 1991-2020 climate normals; media is booked GL spend; KPIs are Service Titan plus client records. n is the number of aligned months.

                                  Why brand awareness matters most in peak season
                                  • Most buyers are in-market during peak season. Share of voice converts to share of market most efficiently when the buying population is largest.
                                  • A live brand makes paid capture cheaper. PPC and LSA auctions are most expensive exactly when demand spikes; a recognized name lifts click-through and lowers effective cost-per-lead in the same window.
                                  • Awareness decays. Top-of-funnel built in the shoulder season is what converts in peak. The mind-share you bought in March is the demand you harvest in July.
                                  • Peak season is the best new-customer window. Acquisition tracks media more than weather. First-time customer counts move with branded search and recent media flights, not with temperature.
                                  • The play: keep your foot on the gas. Peak season is prime fishing season. You land far more new customers when the water is full, so push spend up and out-fish the competition rather than coast on the weather. Govern it with share-of-demand and cost-per-new-customer.

                                  Peak season is defined per market. Sacramento and Chico-Redding peak in summer cooling. San Francisco peaks in the heating and shoulder months. The play is the same; the calendar shifts.

                                  Sources. Weather: NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 monthly climate normals, stations KSFO, KSAC, KRDD; degree days base 65F. Operating data: Service Titan Jobs Completed plus Marketing Campaign Summary. New customers: Service Titan Customer Report (flag "New"). Brand searches: Google Keyword Planner per-market keyword set. Media spend: GL marketing detail by category.

                                  Why Legit, the engagement case

                                  Why Bonney's go-forward marketing and consulting work should sit with Legit as a single, full-suite partner. Written for the leadership conversation that follows Kelly's review.

                                  The thesis

                                  In a PE-active home-services market, the company needs ONE partner that runs the marketing operation AND advises on strategic value preservation. Stacking three or four specialist vendors (a creative shop, a media buyer, an SEO firm, a strategic consultant) creates blind spots, reporting friction, and transition risk in a diligence process. A single all-encompassing partner with 8 years of Bonney context is a defensible operating advantage and a real EBITA-quality input. This dashboard is the proof of capability; the next step is a full-suite engagement.

                                  The three pressures making this decision time-sensitive

                                  Three category shifts are simultaneously compressing the window where a stable, integrated marketing operation defends valuation. Each one alone is manageable; together they reward a single, accountable partner.

                                  PE consolidation is mid-cycle in HVAC and plumbing

                                  Service Champions (Odyssey), ARS (GI Partners), Apex Service Partners (Alpine), Wrench Group (Leonard Green), and a dozen smaller roll-ups are buying. The Bonney family is the right size to be acquired or to acquire. In either path, EBITA quality and marketing-data discipline are priced. Stacked-vendor sprawl is a discount; integrated reporting is a premium.

                                  AI search is moving share off Google

                                  Single-digit but growing share of high-intent home-services buyers now open ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or Apple Intelligence before going to a search bar. The brands that earn AI shelf-space now will own it when the share doubles. This work is editorial, technical, and ongoing, not a one-time SEO project; it requires a partner who can coordinate content, structured data, listings, and PR.

                                  Mass-media-to-search hand-off is misread by most agencies

                                  The Weather vs Demand tab shows what the Bonney family already has: family-wide r=0.50 to 0.61 between marketing spend and revenue / new customers, and a 28% YoY revenue lift in December at constant weather. Mass media creates demand; PPC and LSAs capture it. A marketing partner that does not understand both halves prices the brand as if it had no organic pull.
